en: The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Seven Stars of the Northern Dipper,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Vajrabodhi of South India.
At that time, the Tathāgata, for the sake of all sentient beings of meager merit in the final age, spoke this mantra.
At that time, all the suns, moons, and constellations gathered like clouds, surrounding him from before and behind.
With one voice and in unison, they addressed him, saying:
"We pray only that the Tathāgata will expound for us a divine mantra.
Thereupon, the World-Honored One spoke the mantra of the Eight Stars, saying:
Oṃ saptanarāyaṇabhañja-miñja-rajña-pratimā svāminā rakṣa va-badhu svāhā. This seal and mantra appear in the "Chapter on the Seven Stars" of the *Vajraśekhara Sūtra*.
The Buddha addressed Tanlang, Pujun, and the others, saying:
"If there are good men or good women who receive and uphold this divine mantra, will you protect them?"
Then the eight daughters addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"If there is anyone who recites this divine mantra every day,
their karmic offenses will certainly be entirely extinguished."
All wishes and aspirations shall be fulfilled.
Furthermore, if there should be anyone who can recite this divine mantra one hundred and eight times every day.
One will immediately obtain protection for oneself and all one's retinue.
If one can recite it five hundred times,
its great majestic power [will manifest].
Within five hundred yojanas,
they completely surrounded him;
all the Māra kings and their hosts of demons were there.
All obstructors and immeasurable evil spirits shall not dare to approach;
they shall always provide protection and guardianship.
The eight goddesses of the Northern Dipper, all the suns, moons, lunar mansions, devas, nāgas, and yakṣas—
those who are able to create obstacles and difficulties— are simultaneously severed and destroyed.
If there are those who wish to make offerings, [they should do so].
First, generate the mind of liberation and deliverance;
then, in a pure and tranquil place,
make offerings of incense, flowers, food, and drink.
While reciting the divine mantra and forming the mudrās,
at the time of making such offerings,
the eight goddesses and all their retinues [will appear].
Manifesting in person, one serves according to one's will;
immeasurable aspirations and requests are fulfilled,
and the rank of *jyeṣṭha* (the eldest/foremost) is immediately attained.
How much more so regarding the minor honors of worldly official rank!
If one seeks long life, the registers of fixed karma are erased and replaced with the registers of birth.
If kings, princes, ministers, members of the harem,
and others should construct a maṇḍala within their own palaces and perform homa,
prostrations, and offerings according to the ritual rules.
The eight daughters of the Northern Dipper were all greatly delighted;
thus they long dwelt in their exalted positions, constantly enjoying peace and happiness.
The officials, from high to low, were harmonious and concordant, and no unlawful acts were committed.
The population flourished and the harvests were abundant.
The land was peaceful and secure, free from calamities and the manifestation of strange portents.
Epidemics and deaths did not arise.
Within its borders, hostile enemies and bands of robbers will naturally disperse and retreat.
Therefore, this Dharma is extremely secret;
do not propagate it recklessly among those who lack faith or wisdom.
Because those who lack wisdom do not clearly understand the mind,
they fail to grasp the meaning of the Dharma and give rise to doubt and slander;
this applies even to those such as Vajrasena and Vajraputra, despite their wisdom.
One who constantly recites and upholds the Vidyā of Buddhalocanā should propagate it.
Even though the Vajra-son lacks wisdom, because he does not give rise to doubt or slander, he accomplishes the Dharma.
Although the practitioner may delight in worldly pleasures, [he shall attain success].
They dedicate deeply toward unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
